newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW -- Optimism seen for China power companies.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW -- Optimism seen for China power companies.

text.p: China's power suppliers are poised for solid growth in the years ahead, but poor reception of H-shares might force some companies to postpone any intention of listing in Hong Kong, analysts said.
In order to attract investors, analysts said some issuers might be forced to lower their offering prices, which might then deny them adequate funds.
"It may affect their listing plans because the price to earnings multiple may have to be lowered to attract interest," analyst Chan Man Lung with China Everbright Securities said.
But he added such companies "are good long-term investments due to their steady growth and secure earnings when many of their projects have guaranteed consumption".
Mainland companies such as Datang Power, Zhou Xian Power Plant and De Zhou Power Plant Co are expected to seek H-share listings in coming months.

"We are optimistic over the long-term earnings prospects of the (power supply) industry due to an overall shortage of power supply in China which can provide steady earnings growth," said Wilson Chow, an analyst from Nomura Research.
In a recent research report, ING Barings analyst Johnny Wong said demand for electricity in China was expected to continue growing as Beijing eased credit controls.
Maurien Yau, senior analyst at DBS Securities, agreed. "They do have (good) earnings potential in the longer term because most areas (in China) have an undersupply of power."
But analysts also added the success of a stock issue would depend on where a company's operations were based.
"It would be seen as more attractive if the projects were in high-growth areas, such as industrial zones or densely populated areas," said Kinson Au, senior analyst from PW Asia Brokerage.
"Companies serving these areas are likely to provide better growth potential," he said.
Analysts said IPOs in the power supply business would broaden the range of mainland China companies listed in Hong Kong and generally agreed that they should raise interest.
"I think they will be welcomed in the market. It can provide more choice in the (H-share) market where existing counters are mainly involved in the petrochemical industry," said Chow.
"Red-chips are also seen to be expensive," he added.
Red chips are China-backed, Hong Kong-based companies which are listed on the Hong Kong bourse.
Analysts said highway-related new listings may also diversify the H-share market and have strong earnings potential.

"Toll roads and highway concerns are seen to have more upside in earnings as traffic is hard to control while power plants are always under administrative control relating to cost and quantity which limit earnings growth," Yau said.
However, analyst said it was easier to forecasts earnings for power suppliers than toll road operators.
"Their (power supplier) earnings are normally easier to estimated due to guaranteed consumption. And that enables them to have better transparency, especially on earnings," said Chan.
